specification.title: A migration whose reversal deletes its marker
steps: Runner A applies { m1 }. m1 inserts marker m1.
Revert with the framework's default selection. m1's reversal deletes marker m1.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the revert has returned and the reapply has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: If a revert reports a migration as reverted, its history entry is absent and its marker is absent.

execution.description: Positive control. Explicit BEGIN, parameterized writes, COMMIT or ROLLBACK. PG::Result#cmd_status of COMMIT must be COMMIT before the control reports committed. A tag of ROLLBACK is reported as rolled back. Any other tag, or a COMMIT that raises, is reported as failed. A failed ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT is followed by ROLLBACK, not COMMIT. A connection whose ROLLBACK failed is closed. BEGIN carries a requested isolation level. One PG::Connection, or a one-connection holder for TX-03. Not a framework pool.

configuration.commit_reply: cmd_status checked; only COMMIT is a commit, only ROLLBACK is a rollback

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: A reported revert says the migration's effects are gone. The next apply is what shows that history and the database agree: the migration runs again.

api_outcome.contract: The correct control runs a migration in one transaction. It takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock, then creates its history table if it is missing, before it reads history, applies the migration only when history has no entry, and commits the marker and the history entry together. A reversal deletes the marker and the history entry, refuses a migration that has no reversal, and rolls back a reversal that raises.
